C-AGENT-TOOL-CONTRACTS.Summary: Make every vvoc-owned agent tool expose a complete, runtime-consistent public contract: explicit input schemas, non-lossy validation, actionable diagnostics, checked responses, trustworthy workflow inspection, and synchronized instructions and examples.
C-AGENT-TOOL-CONTRACTS.Problem: Workflow tool schemas leave known structures and enums opaque while handlers enforce additional rules, sometimes discarding the invalid value or its diagnostic before returning an aggregate error. Some normalization silently removes unknown authority stages or reserved stops, changing the submitted meaning instead of rejecting it. Agents consequently cannot reliably distinguish incorrect arguments, invalid workflow state, missing authority, and unavailable host context from the public interface. Existing instructions, schemas, domain validators, and result views provide parts of the contract, but their completeness and agreement are not verified as an end-to-end agent-facing API.

Goals.Goal: Enable ordinary tool use, state inspection, and correction of a rejected call from the public interface without reverse-engineering installed JavaScript or private TypeScript types.
Cover all nine existing vvoc-owned tools and every supported action, decision, command, and nested operation with explicit public input and result contracts.
Reject invalid or contradictory input without silently dropping constraints, changing intent, consuming authority, or authorizing side effects.
Make runtime state and safe next steps inspectable while preserving existing authorization, workflow, editing, and transport safety properties.
Keep schemas, runtime validation, examples, managed instructions, and published reference material consistent through executable contract checks.

Constraints.Constraint: The tool scope is work_item_open, work_item_list, work_item_close, work_item_decide, work_checkpoint, hashline_edit, str_replace_editor, web_search, and web_fetch. The tracked subagent prompt/result protocol is also in scope. Host-owned tools and third-party MCP contracts are outside this change except for testing vvoc integration boundaries.

Preserve existing tool names, orchestration profiles, per-model edit routing, registration and visibility rules, root-session authorization, and supported requirement sources. Prefer the current tool surface and read-only inspection path over adding a second API or one new tool per action.

Separate public structural contracts from state-dependent domain rules and trusted host context. A schema-valid request is not authorization, proof of evidence, a passing review, or permission for a state transition.

The public generic execution descriptor accepts only conversation-scoped and provided-plan sources. Internal native-package records, trusted workspace roots, host identities, reviewer outcomes, and authority eligibility must not become caller-supplied shortcuts around existing checks.

Use the pinned OpenCode plugin schema API and existing project patterns. Reuse canonical enums, bounds, and pure contract rules without introducing runtime import cycles or coupling the dependency-free common workflow contract to the plugin SDK.

Preserve intended valid calls and documented defaults. Rejection of formerly ignored unknown fields, invalid values, contradictory fields, or lossy coercions is an intentional validation tightening and must be documented, tested, and distinguished from changes to workflow semantics.

Preserve work-item identity, idempotency, session isolation, native source validation, review obligations and freshness, ordinary attempt/generation limits, finite authority reserves, replay protection, reserved stops, and fail-closed persistence and recovery behavior.

Preserve supported persisted state and its history without resets, invented permissions, or a gratuitous snapshot migration. A public tool-contract revision must not silently redefine the persistence version or canonical vvoc config schema.

Validation ordering must preserve each operation's transaction boundary. Structural rejection precedes business mutation; domain rejection preserves the established item-level or execution-level atomicity contract rather than imposing a new universal batch behavior.

Diagnostics and inspection remain bounded and permission-aware. Do not echo arbitrary sensitive payloads, expose foreign-session records, or fetch private authorization-message contents merely to explain an error.

Use synthetic fixtures and isolated stores/workspaces for regression evidence. Do not copy private session history into repository artifacts or make access to a user's OpenCode database a prerequisite for tests.

Do not modify user-owned configuration, installed global agents or skills, credentials, model presets, release automation, or archived change bundles. Preserve install/sync and restart semantics; dist remains generated output.

The specification does not assert a universal reduction in model errors or package-source reads. Deterministic contract evidence and observed live-host behavior must be distinguished from unmeasured model effectiveness.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No prohibition on reading package sources, suppression of legitimate enforcement audits, or instruction telling agents to continue blindly after an unexplained refusal.
No replacement of the workflow state machine with JSON Schema, relaxation of permissions or hard stops, automatic acceptance, unbounded retries, or broader report repair.

No universal filesystem sandbox for writeScope and no semantic verification that free-form evidence proves a claim. Document existing enforcement boundaries honestly rather than adding or promising unrelated guarantees.

No rewrite of all plugins, CLI commands, configuration schemas, public library exports, provider integrations, or persistence formats. Existing correct contracts receive coverage rather than cosmetic restructuring.
No forced JSON conversion of human-readable edit/web content or binary attachments, and no claim that OpenCode automatically exposes output schemas to the model.
No large always-loaded protocol manual, new documentation service, usage-analytics project, telemetry rollout, or model benchmark platform.
No implementation, plan.xml, package release, installation, or commit as part of specification authoring.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AC-01: A test-backed public contract inventory covers all nine tools and their supported branches: work-item modes and registration/append paths; every work_item_decide decision and work_checkpoint action, including source-specific variants; hashline edit operations; str_replace_editor commands; and web search/fetch options. Each operation records inputs, defaults, conditional requirements, unknown-field policy, state/host prerequisites, result variants, and representative failures.

AC-02: Published input schemas describe all known nested request structures and closed vocabularies, including execution sources, tasks, checkpoints, modes, reviewer roles, and authority stages. Known domain structures are not represented as arbitrary records, any, or unknown. Genuine opaque content or extension points have a documented boundary and an explicit coverage exception, not a blanket exemption for a tool.

AC-03: Field-level schema descriptions state the semantics that a caller needs before invoking the tool: identity purpose and provenance, path kind, bounds, defaults, and branch-specific conditions. Schemas carry representable enums, bounds, and structures; conditions unsupported by the host's schema subset remain explicitly described and runtime-validated rather than falsely claimed to be encoded.

AC-04: Runtime validation and the public contract agree on required, optional, and incompatible fields for each mode, action, decision, and source path. In particular, execution and runId remain mutually exclusive for work_item_open, append operations require their amendment context, source-specific checkpoint operations retain their own prerequisites, and requiredReviewers rules are not flattened into one incorrect rule for all modes.

AC-05: The generic execution source has explicit conversation-scoped and provided-plan variants; provided-plan requires its bounded reference and validates optional fields when present. An unsupported kind, absent reference, or invalid optional value is rejected with the precise source field identified. Supplying native-package through this descriptor does not bypass native plan/spec loading and validation.

AC-06: Path contracts distinguish exact workspace-relative files from declared directory subtrees and other tool-specific path kinds. Workflow writeScope rejects wildcards, absolute/home/drive paths, backslashes, traversal, empty segments, and file trailing separators; boundary.directories preserves its established normalization of one trailing separator. Containment failures identify the offending scope and applicable boundary without advising unauthorized scope expansion.

AC-07: Unknown properties in vvoc-controlled request objects are rejected before they can be silently stripped and before business mutation. Exceptions are permitted only for explicitly documented opaque or extensible data regions. Recognized fields that conflict with the selected operation are diagnosed instead of being silently ignored. The actual host validation path is covered, not only direct handler calls.

AC-08: Normalization is explicit, bounded, and meaning-preserving: retain documented trimming, defaults, and path canonicalization, but do not stringify arbitrary values, turn invalid collections into empty ones, drop invalid optional fields, or filter unrecognized enum values into an apparently valid request. Public structural rules, runtime validators, and generated or checked examples share canonical definitions or executable agreement checks.

AC-09: An unknown or misspelled authority stage or reserved stop, alone or mixed with valid entries, rejects the complete proposed authority operation. The regression reservedStops=["verificaton"] cannot create or modify an authority, omit the requested stop silently, claim its authorization message, consume or replenish reserve, or expose new launch/stage permissions.

AC-10: Invalid structural input causes no tool business mutation, file edit, provider request, or budget consumption. Standalone work-item batches retain their documented item-level domain outcomes after structural validation; generic execution mutations remain atomic. Tests distinguish whole-request structural rejection from supported per-item domain rejection and demonstrate the corresponding absence or isolation of side effects.

AC-11: Workflow validation failures expose a stable machine-readable error identity and category, a precise argument path when applicable, the violated expectation, and a bounded human-readable explanation. Nested arrays include the relevant item index or identity. Compatible existing codes are retained where their meaning remains correct; more specific additive details replace aggregate messages that conceal the failing condition.

AC-12: Caller-input, workflow-state, authorization, trusted-host-context, and persistence failures are distinguishable. A missing trusted workspace root or plan loader is not reported as an invitation to change unrelated caller fields. Invalid execution.source.kind does not mention missing workspace context when that context is valid. A failed generic lookup is not disguised as missing native-only arguments.

AC-13: State-dependent refusals identify the current applicable state and unmet prerequisite, with a safe next step or explicit stop when one is known. This covers premature close, wrong or unavailable attempt, conditional concernsDisposition, exhausted budgets, pending or failed review, and unavailable authority. Guidance does not silently accept work, authorize recovery, remove obligations, recreate identity to reset counters, or promise that a suggested action will remain valid after concurrent state changes.

AC-14: All owned structured success and failure result variants have executable contracts and serialization coverage, including nested workflow views and batch outcomes. Web and edit text, metadata, and attachment envelopes have explicit declared shapes while arbitrary document content remains opaque. Existing text/attachment delivery and permission behavior remain usable; output schemas are a producer/test contract, not an assumed model-visible SDK feature. A serialization or result-contract failure after side effects must not be misreported as a pre-execution input rejection or invite unsafe replay; preserve truthful commit/failure semantics.

AC-15: work_item_list provides same-session inspection of standalone work items and both generic and native executions through stable public views. A controller can recover execution/work-item identities, current attempt or generation and terminal status, acceptance/review prerequisites, and applicable budget/recovery information needed for a decision without private store inspection. Existing includeClosed behavior remains defined, and foreign-session data is not exposed.

AC-16: Inspection and mutation responses provide consistent state-derived next-action/precondition information where applicable, reusing the domain's actual eligibility rules instead of a separate optimistic decision table. BLOCKED, NEEDS_CONTEXT, rejected reports, exhausted allowances, and unavailable authorization remain distinguishable. Inspecting state or describing a recovery path neither grants recovery nor consumes a unit.

AC-17: A read-only public workflow inspection result identifies the running plugin package version and public tool-contract revision from the loaded implementation, not from an unrelated global installation, mutable config entry, or latest remote documentation. Version-specific reference material is discoverable from shipped descriptions or managed references. The information remains consistent with startup snapshot and restart behavior.

AC-18: The tracked launch/result protocol is specified separately from tool argument schemas and checked against the parsers. Instructions and executable examples cover exact returned work-item identity, role-appropriate statuses, required fields, top-block/body separation, and bounded report continuation. A fixed sample wi-1 is not presented as the value to reuse for every task.

AC-19: Wrong identity is not repaired by silently substituting the expected ID, and malformed BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT reports do not become success or enter broader automatic continuation. Existing same-child repair eligibility, attempt identity, bounded excerpts, and terminal report-rejection/recovery semantics are preserved and remain inspectable at the public boundary.

AC-20: Tool descriptions, workflow system guidance, managed agent/skill templates, and README agree on the public contract and the distinction between schema validation, runtime enforcement, and controller judgment. Common invocation requirements are available without loading an execution skill; longer reference material is on demand and packaged with the matching release. Executable examples are generated from or validated against the same contracts.

AC-21: hashline_edit and str_replace_editor expose complete operation-specific requirements, anchor/range semantics, allowed content forms, and documented errors without changing literal edit behavior, stale-anchor protection, model routing, or host permission checks. web_search and web_fetch expose their options, bounds, defaults, formats, URL expectations, and errors without leaking provider-specific credentials or changing provider-neutral delivery.

AC-22: Correct standalone, delegated, generic, and native workflow scenarios retain their existing successful behavior and safety gates. Tests cover idempotent replay, cross-session/control denial, source-switch rejection, skipped or stale review, conditional concerns disposition, finite recovery, authority replay/revocation, persistence failure, and supported state hydration. Schema acceptance and next-action guidance cannot substitute for any of these gates.

AC-23: Contract tests exercise the actual registered tool definitions and model-facing JSON Schema projection, not only TypeScript types or helper validators. SDK-shaped fixtures test parsing, dispatch, serialization, and host-originated validation failures. At least one positive and one relevant negative fixture covers every public operation branch; unknown nested properties and lossy-normalization counterexamples are included.

AC-24: Mandatory diagnostic regressions cover source.kind="conversation", provided-plan without reference, invalid nested task/checkpoint input, file-versus-directory paths, OUT_OF_BOUNDARY, reservedStops=["verificaton"], unexpected and required concernsDisposition, premature close, wrong work-item identity, and malformed hard-stop reports. Each input failure identifies the actionable cause, and stateful scenarios assert the material safety property rather than merely checking an error string.

AC-25: The derived plan defines a bounded transport-compatibility matrix from the supported OpenCode SDK/host contract and representative provider serialization paths. Evidence includes generated-schema checks and a focused isolated OpenCode smoke exercising exposed definitions and accepted/rejected calls. Local Zod parsing alone is not evidence of provider compatibility; unexercised host/provider combinations and unavailable live checks are reported explicitly.

AC-26: A repository check included in bun run check detects an unregistered public tool/action in the contract coverage inventory, undocumented opaque request structures, and drift between checked examples, schemas, runtime branches, and result variants. Adding a tool or action requires a contract, example, and negative scenario rather than relying on reviewers to notice an incomplete declaration.

AC-27: Compatibility documentation identifies stricter validation of previously ignored/coerced inputs, any intentional error classification changes, and the additive inspection/result fields. Public package exports, user configuration, persisted history, and installed assets are not silently migrated. Bundled reference assets and contract metadata are verified in the package surface; updates still require the documented sync/restart workflow.

AC-28: Implementation updates README, affected file-local contracts, owning graph/verification projections, and scenario coverage inside the approved lifecycle. Baselines in the derived plan are behavior-sensitive; spec grammar validation is not implementation evidence. Contract and reference size are inspected so completeness does not become a full manual injected on every turn.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: bun test src/lib/workflow-contract.test.ts src/plugins/workflow/authority.test.ts src/plugins/workflow/delegated.test.ts src/plugins/workflow/checkpoints.test.ts src/plugins/workflow/execution.test.ts src/plugins/workflow/persistence.test.ts src/plugins/workflow/transactions.test.ts
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The plan adds focused public-contract/schema/result tests and wires the coverage guard into the standard check. Existing suites above are regression gates, not substitutes for those new tests. A wire-schema fixture and an actual plugin/host boundary scenario must accompany each materially different validation route.

Authority counterexamples assert unchanged authority records, message claims, reserves, and eligibility after invalid requests. Other negative scenarios assert unchanged files, no provider dispatch, or the established workflow transaction outcome. Positive flows demonstrate retained functionality rather than merely rejecting more inputs.

A bounded compatibility record names SDK/host versions, exercised provider-schema transformations, successful and rejected sandbox calls, result-contract coverage, and remaining gaps. Synthetic authorization lookup tests prove handler behavior only and are not reported as live authorization or transport evidence.

Packaged references and runtime-reported identity are checked against the built release inputs. Prompt/example checks demonstrate consistency, not measured model quality. No pass criterion depends on the private historical read counts or on zero intentional source-code audits.

Assumptions.Assumption: The user-approved discussion direction covers all vvoc-owned agent tools, not every public CLI/config/library surface or third-party tool. Nine tool names are the current inventory; discovery of additional owned tools must be resolved explicitly rather than silently omitted.

Stricter rejection of unknown, contradictory, or invalid input is the proposed compatibility trade-off. It preserves intended valid behavior but intentionally stops accepting requests whose constraints were previously ignored or coerced.

Exact schema composition, diagnostic field names, contract-revision representation, reference packaging, and the compatibility test harness are implementation-plan decisions. They cannot relax the acceptance criteria or change public tool names, persisted semantics, or host safety boundaries without an explicit scope decision.

The original report motivates the change; its historical counts and per-session causal attribution have not been independently reproduced. The aggregate source error and dropped reserved-stop counterexample were reproduced with isolated in-memory handlers, which does not establish all historical causes or live-provider behavior.
